narrative.title: Probing One Pin of the Badge Register
narrative.scenario: A security badge encodes its zones as an integer, and the gate reader must ask whether one specific pin — counted from the least significant pin starting at zero — is currently carrying voltage. Shifting the register right by the pin's index parks that pin in the last slot, where a single AND with one reveals its state.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n and a 0-based bit index k.
narrative.outputFormat: true when the k-th bit of n is set, false otherwise.

testCases.explanation: 4 is 100; the least significant pin carries no voltage.
The only set pin of 100 sits at index 2.

hintLevels: Level 1: Two equivalent probes — mask the pin (n & (1 << k)) or slide it to the front (n >> k) & 1.
Level 2: Both run in constant time; the shift form reads more naturally when the caller already wants a boolean.
Level 3: Watch the indexing convention: this problem is 0-based from the LSB, unlike its 1-based sibling.
